mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which typically supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS shows a sustained upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy stance that increases discount rates for equities, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market amid monetary tightening, which typically causes equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market strength
failure_condition: The interaction between FEDFUNDS and UNRATE fails to predict negative returns, with Rank IC below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansion when HOUST declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand and economic activity, which typically supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST shows a sustained upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A supply-demand imbalance where industrial production (INDPRO) growth outpaces GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates overcapacity and weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction between INDPRO and GDPC1 fails to predict negative returns, with Rank IC below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, which typically causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS rises.
